notes: §1985:VIII.4.6.4 GR5: REWRITE ... FROM identifier-1 'is equivalent to the execution of the following statements in the order specified': MOVE identifier-1 TO record-name-1 under the MOVE rules, then the same REWRITE without FROM; the 1985 format admits only identifier-1 (§1985:VIII.4.6.2). MoveBinder.BindFromPhrase binds the implicit MOVE from the FromPhraseRules.Rewrite row (MOVE validity), the keyed/sequential emitters run it before the rewrite on every path, and VersionConformancePass.VisitRecordFromPhrase refuses the 2002 FROM literal-1 at 85 (COBOL0871). Witness: shorter, longer and numeric FROM operands padded, truncated and zero-filled. Probes (d,f): S9(3)V9 -12.5 to a PIC 9(6) record 000012; edited ZZ9.99 to PIC X 1.50; S9(3)V9 to a group record as a group move 012N; OCCURS DEPENDING group (WC=2) padded AB; FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (alphanumeric function) ABCDEF; subscripted TE(I). (e): REWRITE before OPEN 49 and random REWRITE of an absent record 23, the MOVE done first in both (RA=abcdef). (c,b): FROM "ABC", SPACES, ALL "X", 12 each COBOL0871; FUNCTION LENGTH refused COBOL1914; empty FROM and FROM written twice refused; INVALID KEY on a sequential relative REWRITE refused COBOL1720.

next.reason: 2023 adds FROM literal-1 (§2023:14.9.35.4 GR7: "MOVE literal-1 TO record-name-1"), which the 1985 format refuses; the FROM identifier-1 case is unchanged. §2023:14.9.35.4 GR7 keeps the equivalence: MOVE identifier-1 TO record-name-1 per the MOVE rules, then 'The same REWRITE statement without the FROM phrase'; §2023:14.9.35.3 SR6 states the MOVE-validity part ('shall be valid as a sending operand in a MOVE statement'). Literal-1 is new syntax only.
